headline: Learned models predict protein-ligand and protein-protein binding from structure
label: Machine Learning Binding Prediction
summary: Co-folding foundation models and graph transformers are now applied to affinity, enzyme-substrate, and antibody-antigen prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned representations of protein and ligand structure applied to binding and interaction prediction. Several items target small-molecule and ligand affinity or screening: DrugCLIP frames virtual screening as contrastive embedding retrieval, and DBGT-PLA pairs a dual-branch graph-transformer with edge-level Shapley attribution. Others extend this logic to protein-protein and antibody-antigen interactions: PreFold-dG estimates ΔG from intermediate embeddings of the Boltz-2 structure model, and Chai-1 gains B-cell epitope predictor restraints for antibody-antigen modeling. Boltz2ESI applies co-folding to enzyme-substrate interactions without predefined pockets. What is new is the use of foundation-model co-folding embeddings and pocket-free inputs as features, epitope-informed restraints, and attribution-based interpretability, rather than sequence-only models. The remaining items, covering backbone generation, design steering, kinase variant scoring, and proteome-scale simulation, are related methodological work rather than direct binding prediction.
